summary:
## Vision: Astronaut Health Monitoring and Wellness Prototype

Vision is an open-source, local-first prototype designed to help astronauts record and review health indicators during space missions. Individual crew accounts use Supabase authentication and store check-ins for heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, and mood. The dashboard presents recent readings and personal trends, while routines support mission-time scheduling, reminders, and completion tracking. Browser-based caching and an offline outbox help preserve check-ins during connectivity interruptions.

The J.A.R.V.I.S. assistant provides conversational wellness support using MedGemma through local Ollama. Optional Gradium speech services enable voice transcription and spoken replies, with controls for silent mode and interrupting responses. The interface also presents NASA DONKI solar activity reports and links to NASA Human Research Program resources about spaceflight hazards. Environmental reports are clearly distinguished from personal radiation measurements.

Vision is a research and demonstration prototype, not a medical device or NASA-endorsed system. It does not diagnose or replace mission procedures, medical officers, or flight surgeons.
details:
Vision is an open-source prototype for astronaut health monitoring and wellness support during long-duration missions. It lets crew members record heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, and mood; review recent readings and personal trends; and manage routines and reminders. An integrated J.A.R.V.I.S. assistant provides conversational wellness support, while NASA DONKI reports offer space-weather context. These reports are clearly distinguished from personal radiation-dose measurements.


Dependencies and requirements

  • Web app: Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+, npm, and a modern browser.
  • Accounts and health-data storage: A configured Supabase project with authentication, crew_profiles and health_readings tables, appropriate row-level security, and the user-profile trigger. The frontend uses a Supabase publishable key.
  • Local assistant: Ollama with the MedGemma model installed. Hardware needs depend on the model variant and local system; Vision does not require dedicated biomedical sensors.
  • Optional voice: Python 3.10+, pip, the packages listed in voice-requirements.txt, a Gradium API key, and microphone access for spoken input. Voice services require internet access.
  • NASA context: Internet access to NASA DONKI; the prototype currently uses NASA’s public demo API key.
  • Offline behavior: Check-ins may be cached and queued locally when the connection is unavailable, then synced after reconnection. Supabase and Gradium features require connectivity.
  • Programming: Codex, ChatGPT, CLAUDE AND Gemini
  • Repository: Github
  • Presentation: Gamma
